# ImageDecodeFailureUnchecked

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Decoding image bytes can fail and return false. Check the result before using it as an image.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$im=imagecreatefromstring($bytes); imagepng($im);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Check image decoding success before using the image.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- D1. A local directly assigned resolved imagecreatefromstring is consumed as first argument of imagepng/imagejpeg/imagegif/imagesx/imagesy without a false-result guard. Require unknown input or known invalid literal bytes.
- D1a. A guard is a test of the same variable while it still holds that decode result. Accepted tests: plain truthiness (`$im`, `!$im`, `empty($im)`), strict or loose comparison with `false`, `instanceof`, `is_object`, `is_resource`, `is_bool`, and the decode assignment tested in place (`if (!$im = imagecreatefromstring($b))`). Tests combine through `!`, `&&`/`and` and `||`/`or` with their usual logic: a conjunction that holds proves each operand, a disjunction that fails refutes each operand.
- D1b. A guard protects a use when the use sits in the branch the test selects (if/elseif/else arm, including arms reached only after an earlier condition of the chain failed; ternary arm; right operand of a short-circuit operator), or when an earlier statement of the same or an enclosing statement list leaves the path on failure: an `if` without `elseif` whose failing arm always terminates (return, throw, exit, break, continue), `test or exit/throw`, `!test and exit/throw`, or `assert(test)`.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods; user-defined lookalikes are excluded. Follow only bounded local proof in one lexical scope.
- D3. Emit one finding per violating operation, not per supporting evidence statement. Use existing analysis budgets; exhausted proof produces no report.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Do not report unresolved or shadowed builtin names, unknown values, or incomplete receiver/type provenance. Unknown calls, aliases escaping, and intervening writes invalidate local proof. Similar code outside the stated detection contract is not a finding.
- E2. Both standard suppression forms suppress this native ID.
- E3. A guard on an earlier decode result does not cover a later reassignment, and a guard whose failing arm merely logs or calls an ordinary function does not protect the following code: both are still reported.
- E4. Guards expressed indirectly stay unrecognised and are reported: `match (true)` arms, and exceptions thrown and caught inside the same function.
- E5. A value the shared flow analysis proves is not the failure value at the use is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: a test in an enclosing branch, loop condition or short-circuit operand, an early exit, a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$v !== false or exit;`, `$v or throw …;`, `$v ?: throw …;`), a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables: such a call throws a `TypeError` for `false`. A `switch (true)` case is read like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain; in a `switch` on the variable itself with constant labels, the cases after a `false` or `null` label and the `default` hold a value that is neither, as does a `true` case. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`.

## Fix

None. Choosing a repair requires intent or additional runtime information.

## PHP versions

Available throughout supported PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced builtin/extension is available. Respect syntax/version-specific receiver contracts; unavailable APIs are not this rule’s concern.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ImageDecodeFailureUnchecked": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ImageDecodeFailureUnchecked
```
